messages:
sara: Hey team — getting a customer escalation: intermittent 502/504s hitting Hosted API (edge) during large nightly inference batch. Customer says it started ~01:10 UTC and affects multiple requests in a short window. They gave a trace id: trace=8a3f2c1e and an example request id: req=cc9a4f. They can repro reliably by replaying a 1k-request batch to /v1/generate.

sara: Sample curl they used: 
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" -d @batch.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
They see lots of `upstream prematurely closed connection` and occasional `502` HTML from the gateway.

devon: thx sara. can you paste headers from one of the failing responses? also any envoy/edge trace we can pull?

sara: pasted headers from client capture: 
```
HTTP/2 502
content-type: text/html; charset=UTF-8
date: Mon, 22 Jul 2024 01:11:05 GMT
x-request-id: cc9a4f
x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 212
server: envoy
```
Also copied the customer tcp dump snippet showing RST from upstream at ~01:11:04.

kai: looks like h2 upstream pool exhaustion / stream windowing. we've seen similar when many long-lived streaming responses plus concurrent short requests. envoys' upstream keepalive pools can run out. can you attach the edge logs for that timeframe?

sara: attaching logs (excerpt): 
```
[01:11:03.542] envoy error] upstream connection closed while a request was outstanding, upstream_reset: connection failure
[01:11:03.543] envoy warning] pool capacity exhausted, waiting for healthy upstream
[01:11:04.001] envoy info] selected upstream 10.2.5.11:8000, cluster hosted-inference
```

devon: confirmed pool exhaustion messages. is this the batch traffic hitting a single availability zone? curious if routing concentrated to one pool. can ops add per-pod/host connection counts?

james: i'm oncall. quick mitigations: 1) temporary increase h2 max-concurrent-streams and connection pool size on the edge for cluster hosted-inference (safe for 10m). 2) enable fallback routing to a different region/variant for heavy customers (doable via route rule). 3) throttle the customer's burst in support plan. which do we want first?

maria: customer is high-touch, will accept brief throttling + we prefer a config fix before telling them to change client. they want ETA asap.

devon: I'll try 1) and 2) in parallel. increasing pool sizes now, then flip fallback route. watch metrics: active_conns, pending_streams, envoy upstream resets.

deploy-bot: deploy started by devon: edge-config-change/raise-h2-pool-sizes @ 2024-07-22T01:20:15Z (diff: increase max_connections 100->200, max_streams 100->250)

edge-bot: rolling restart scheduled for 3 edge nodes in zone-1 to pick up new config. rollout ETA ~4m.

james: after the restart, we saw a sharp drop in upstream resets and 502s for customer traffic. monitoring shows x-envoy-upstream-service-time median returned to normal.

maria: customer confirmed improvement after ~01:26 UTC. they still see occasional single-request 502s but overall success rate is back to normal. they've accepted a post-mortem and changes on our side.

kai: root-cause hypothesis: combination of bursty batch traffic + multiple long poll/stream responses consuming multiplexed h2 streams -> pool saturation + connection resets when upstream can't accept new streams. mitigation: 1) tune keepalive + pool sizes, 2) prefer short-lived connections for short requests (connection pooling policy split), 3) adaptive throttling at edge for heavy tail batches, 4) add per-customer rate-limit-exceptions for dedicated customers. also add an alert when pool_exhaustion_rate > 0.5% in 1m.

devon: follow-ups assigned: ENG-RUNTIME to add pool-backed metrics (devon), EDGE infra to add adaptive throttle rule (james), SUPPORT to coordinate rollback plan if we see regressions (sara), CS to confirm customer SLA note (maria). I'll create tickets and link them here.

sara: creating ticket now with traces and repro steps. action items logged. thanks all. :thumbsup:
